On this page

Installing from the Marketplace ​

The Marketplace is Saidi's catalog of MCP servers and skills you can attach to an agent. It aggregates several upstream sources into one searchable list, caches them, and materialises the chosen entry into the target agent's configuration.

Sources ​

SourceProvides
MCP RegistryPublished MCP servers
GitHubServers and skills resolved straight from repos
GlamaIndexed MCP server catalog
Skills marketplaceReusable skill definitions
HTTPAny catalog served as JSON at a URL

Results are normalised into one entry shape and cached, so browsing does not hammer upstream on every keystroke. saidi-marketplace runs the catalog service standalone from Settings → Connections if you want to point at your own.

Install an MCP server ​

From the UI: Marketplace → find the server → Install → pick the target agent.

From chat, the same thing explicitly:

add_mcp_server(agent: "research", name: "notion", config: { ... })

Either way the result is an entry in agents/<name>/.mcp.json. The server is available to that agent only — this is the main reason to give a capability its own agent rather than widening PRIME's toolbelt.

Authentication ​

Many MCP servers need OAuth or an API key.

  • API keys go in the server config, sourced from your secrets store — not pasted into a repo file.
  • OAuth servers need an interactive authorisation once. A server that has never been authorised is unavailable, and a headless or scheduled run cannot complete the flow. Authorise it from an interactive session first.

Saidi probes configured servers to report which are reachable, which are unauthorised, and which are misconfigured, so a broken server shows up as a status rather than as a mysterious tool failure mid-run.

Install a skill ​

import_skill(agent: "research", url: "https://.../pricing-scan.md")
add_skill(agent: "research", name: "competitor-teardown", content: "...")

Skills land in agents/<name>/skills/. A skill is a procedure the agent can invoke by name; it is loaded on demand rather than sitting in the system prompt, so a large library costs nothing until used.

Before you install ​

  • Read what it can reach. An MCP server is a capability grant. A server with write access to a production system belongs on a permission: custom agent with a short tool list, not on one with all.
  • Prefer the narrowest agent. If only one specialist needs it, only that specialist should have it.
  • Check it after install. Run the agent read-only on a trivial task and confirm the tool actually resolves before you plan a run around it.

Removing ​

remove_mcp_server(agent: "research", name: "notion")

This edits the agent's .mcp.json. Removing a server that a saved skill depends on will surface as a tool failure the next time that skill runs — remove both together.
